stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C to enhance its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities. The round reflects a growing emphasis on national security in space, particularly as threats evolve. Investors seem to believe that securing space is as important as securing the ground.
stories.soWhat: It's clear that in the current landscape, cash is king, especially when it comes to defense applications.

stories.head: Intel launches new chip for space computing
stories.body: Intel unveiled its latest chip designed specifically for space computing, aiming to boost satellite data processing speeds. While the exact performance metrics remain under wraps, the chip is expected to outperform traditional systems, which is crucial for real-time data applications in orbit. Given that many satellites still operate on outdated tech, this could shift the market significantly.
stories.soWhat: If Intel can deliver, we might finally see satellites that can process data faster than a 1990s desktop.

stories.head: Palantir wins $480M extension on TITAN program
stories.body: Palantir has secured a $480 million extension for its TITAN ground station program, emphasizing the importance of data integration in military operations. This extension highlights the defense sector's reliance on established tech firms to manage complex data environments. Palantir's continued success raises questions about competition in the space data integration market.
stories.soWhat: This deal reinforces the notion that in defense procurement, familiarity often trumps innovation.

watchlist.title: Amazon's satellite constellation application review
watchlist.body: Amazon's plans for a 5,100-satellite constellation could reshape direct-to-device services, but regulatory hurdles may slow progress.

watchlist.title: Blue Origin's New Glenn tests at Stennis
watchlist.body: Upcoming tests of the New Glenn upper stages could clarify Blue Origin's path to market, especially against SpaceX's established dominance.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser timeline uncertainty
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser DoD variant passing its design review, attention will turn to its launch timeline—will it actually meet expectations?

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: After raising $190 million, True Anomaly's strategy will be crucial in determining how quickly it can scale its co-orbital capabilities.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
